questions.prompt: Join fact_sales to dim_customer for natural customer_id and customer_history at sale time. Return sale_key,customer_id,country as of each order_date.

questions.title: Idempotent incremental UPSERT & stale updates · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Apply incoming_people to current_people with INSERT ON CONFLICT(customer_id) DO UPDATE only if the incoming updated_at is newer. Apply that same batch twice. Return customer_id,name,updated_at.

questions.title: Idempotent incremental UPSERT & stale updates · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Apply that UPSERT once. Return customer_id,customer_key for all current_people rows, showing that old keys stayed stable.

questions.title: Stage, validate & atomically promote a refresh · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Simulate an interrupted promotion: BEGIN, DELETE published_totals, INSERT from refresh_stage, ROLLBACK. Return customer_id,total_sales; the old snapshot must remain.

questions.title: Stage, validate & atomically promote a refresh · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Promote the known-valid refresh_stage in a transaction: DELETE old rows, INSERT staged rows, COMMIT. Return customer_id,total_sales.

questions.title: Protect fact grain when joining versions · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Return country,total_sales using CURRENT customer_history version, for facts with a customer history match. Group by current country.

questions.title: Protect fact grain when joining versions · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Return country,total_sales using the customer_history version effective at each sale date; group by historical country.

questions.title: Capstone: integrated customers to trusted sales · Challenge 1
questions.prompt: Create TEMP integrated_customers using the integration contract, and TEMP built_sales using the Gold validation rules from lesson Gold: dimensions, facts & quality gates. Return customer_id,name,gender,country,sales_lines,total_sales for valid CRM customers with a dimension match; preserve customers with no valid sales as 0 totals.

questions.title: Capstone: integrated customers to trusted sales · Challenge 2
questions.prompt: Create the same two TEMP outputs. Return country,total_sales at integrated country grain, preserving countries with no sales as 0.

questions.title: Shopper contact list
questions.difficultyWhy: One table, two named columns, no filtering.
questions.prompt: Return the name and email of every shopper.

questions.title: Shoppers in the West region
questions.difficultyWhy: A single equality filter on one table.
questions.prompt: Return the id and name of shoppers whose region is West.

questions.title: Catalog from most to least expensive
questions.difficultyWhy: One table and one sort, plus a stated tie-breaker.
questions.prompt: Return the name and price of every catalog item, most expensive first.

questions.title: Orders with no delivery date
questions.difficultyWhy: One IS NULL test on one table.
questions.prompt: Return the id and status of every order whose delivered_date is missing.

questions.title: The three cheapest items
questions.difficultyWhy: One sort plus LIMIT on one table.
questions.prompt: Return the name and price of the 3 cheapest catalog items, cheapest first.

questions.title: Rename a column
questions.prompt: Return each employee's name and salary, naming the salary column annual_salary.

questions.title: Office locations
questions.prompt: Return each department location once (column location).

questions.title: Hired during 2023
questions.difficultyWhy: One inclusive date range on one table.
questions.prompt: Return the name and hired_at of employees hired during 2023.

questions.title: Orders by status
questions.difficultyWhy: One GROUP BY with COUNT on one table.
questions.prompt: Return each order status and how many orders have it (order_count).

questions.title: Items nobody has ordered
questions.difficultyWhy: A LEFT JOIN anti-join between two tables.
questions.prompt: Return the id and name of catalog items that appear on no order line.

questions.title: Repeat shoppers
questions.difficultyWhy: GROUP BY with a HAVING condition on one table.
questions.prompt: Return shopper_id and order_count for shoppers who placed at least 2 orders.

questions.title: Delivered revenue by category
questions.difficultyWhy: Two joins and one SUM per group; no nesting.
questions.prompt: For delivered orders only, return category and revenue: the sum of quantity × unit_price from order_lines.

questions.title: Signups in the last 30 days
questions.difficultyWhy: One table, but the inclusive 30-day window must be worked out.
questions.prompt: Return the name and signup_date of shoppers who signed up in the 30 days ending on 2025-03-31.

questions.title: Emails used more than once
questions.difficultyWhy: String normalisation plus GROUP BY/HAVING on one table.
questions.prompt: Some shoppers share an email once you ignore letter case and surrounding spaces. Return clean_email and shopper_count for every such email used by more than one shopper.

questions.title: Employees and their departments
questions.difficultyWhy: One INNER JOIN on a foreign key.
questions.prompt: Return employee (the employee's name) and department (the department's name) for employees who belong to a department.

questions.title: Every employee, with a department label
questions.difficultyWhy: LEFT JOIN plus COALESCE for the missing side.
questions.prompt: Return employee and department for every employee. Use 'Unassigned' as the department when an employee has none.

questions.title: Find the lamps
questions.difficultyWhy: One LIKE pattern, but case behaviour matters.
questions.prompt: Return the id and name of catalog items whose name contains “lamp” anywhere, in any letter case.

questions.title: Open orders in February and March
questions.difficultyWhy: IN plus BETWEEN combined correctly; operator precedence is the trap.
questions.prompt: Return id, status and order_date for orders that are shipped or processing and were placed from 2025-02-01 through 2025-03-31.

questions.title: Average salary by department
questions.difficultyWhy: One join, one AVG per group, rounding.
questions.prompt: Return department (name) and avg_salary for every department that has at least one employee.

questions.title: Price bands
questions.difficultyWhy: A three-way CASE with exact boundaries.
questions.prompt: Return name and price_band for every catalog item: 'budget' when price is under 25, 'standard' from 25 up to (not including) 100, 'premium' at 100 or more.

questions.title: Active buyers per month
questions.difficultyWhy: Month bucketing plus a distinct count, one table.
questions.prompt: Return month (YYYY-MM) and active_shoppers: how many different shoppers placed at least one non-cancelled order that month.

questions.title: How long did delivery take?
questions.difficultyWhy: One date difference with a NULL guard.
questions.prompt: For delivered orders that have a delivered_date, return id and days_to_deliver: the number of whole days from order_date to delivered_date.

questions.title: Create a wishlist table
questions.difficultyWhy: One CREATE TABLE with a composite key and two inserts.
questions.prompt: Create a table wishlist with shopper_id INTEGER NOT NULL, item_id INTEGER NOT NULL and added_on TEXT, where (shopper_id, item_id) is the primary key. Insert (1, 12, '2025-03-01') and (2, 4, '2025-03-02'), then return all wishlist rows ordered by shopper_id.

questions.title: Reprice the garden range
questions.difficultyWhy: One UPDATE and one DELETE with WHERE, then a SELECT.
questions.prompt: Raise the price of every Garden item by 10%, and delete the item named 'Wall Clock' (it was never sold). Then return id, name and price of all catalog items.

questions.title: Big spenders for their region
questions.difficultyWhy: Aggregate per shopper, then compare with a per-region average (correlated subquery or CTE); NULL regions excluded.
questions.prompt: A shopper's spend is the sum of quantity × unit_price over their delivered orders. Return name, region and spend for shoppers whose spend is greater than the average spend of shoppers in the same region.

questions.title: Monthly revenue after refunds
questions.difficultyWhy: Two child tables at order grain must be aggregated separately to avoid fan-out; NULL refunds must become 0.
questions.prompt: For delivered orders, return month (YYYY-MM of order_date) and net_revenue: line revenue (quantity × unit_price) minus refunds for those orders.

questions.title: Bestsellers within each category
questions.difficultyWhy: Aggregate after a join, then rank within groups with a stated tie rule.
questions.prompt: For non-cancelled orders, total the units (quantity) sold per catalog item. Return category, name, units and category_rank, where rank 1 is the item with the most units in its category.

questions.title: Seven-day rolling active shoppers
questions.difficultyWhy: Deduplicate to daily counts, then a calendar-based (not row-based) window frame over gaps.
questions.prompt: For each date in app_logins, return login_date, active_shoppers (different shoppers who logged in that day) and rolling_7d: the sum of active_shoppers over that date and the 6 calendar days before it.

questions.title: Earning more than the manager
questions.difficultyWhy: Self-join with two roles of the same table and a strict comparison.
questions.prompt: Return employee, employee_salary, manager and manager_salary for employees who earn strictly more than their direct manager.

questions.title: Days with no orders
questions.difficultyWhy: Requires generating a date series (recursive CTE) and an anti-join against it.
questions.prompt: From 2025-03-01 through 2025-03-14, return each day (column day, YYYY-MM-DD) on which no order was placed, earliest first.

questions.title: First order versus latest order
questions.difficultyWhy: Order totals, then picking first and last rows per shopper with explicit tie rules.
questions.prompt: For shoppers with at least two non-cancelled orders, return shopper_id, first_order_value and latest_order_value. An order's value is the sum of its lines' quantity × unit_price.

questions.title: Orders whose payments don't match
questions.difficultyWhy: Two child tables at different grains (lines, split payments) plus missing payments.
questions.prompt: For delivered or shipped orders, return id, order_total (sum of quantity × unit_price), paid_total (sum of payments) and balance (order_total − paid_total) where paid_total differs from order_total.

questions.title: Order status mix by region
questions.difficultyWhy: Pivot with conditional aggregation across a join, plus a NULL group label.
questions.prompt: Return region and four columns — delivered, shipped, processing, cancelled — counting the orders of shoppers in that region with each status.

questions.title: Loyal shoppers who never needed a refund
questions.difficultyWhy: Combines a counted EXISTS-style condition with a NOT EXISTS across two hops.
questions.prompt: Return the id and name of shoppers who have at least two delivered orders and have never received a refund on any of their orders.

questions.title: Average order value by month
questions.difficultyWhy: The average must be over orders, not lines — a two-step aggregation.
questions.prompt: For delivered orders, return month (YYYY-MM of order_date) and avg_order_value: the average of each order's total (sum of quantity × unit_price).

questions.title: Payroll versus budget
questions.difficultyWhy: LEFT JOIN aggregation with zero-filled groups and a strict comparison.
questions.prompt: For every department, return department, headcount, payroll (sum of salaries) and status: 'over' when payroll exceeds the budget, otherwise 'within'.

questions.title: Keep one account per email
questions.difficultyWhy: Normalisation plus a ranked pick per group with a tie-breaker.
questions.prompt: Treat emails as equal after trimming spaces and lowercasing. For each email, keep the shopper who signed up first. Return id, name and clean_email for the kept shoppers.

questions.title: A covering index for unit totals
questions.difficultyWhy: Requires understanding composite index column order, verified on the built index.
questions.prompt: The report “units sold per item” reads order_lines.item_id and quantity. Create an index named idx_lines_item_qty on order_lines that starts with item_id and also contains quantity, so SQLite can answer from the index alone. Then return item_id and units (sum of quantity) per item.

questions.title: A reusable shopper totals view
questions.difficultyWhy: A view over a join that must count orders, not lines; checked on the view's definition.
questions.prompt: Create a view shopper_order_totals with columns shopper_id, orders (number of non-cancelled orders) and total_spend (sum of quantity × unit_price over those orders, 2 decimals). Then return the view's rows where total_spend is above 150.

questions.title: Second-highest salary per department
questions.difficultyWhy: Distinct values, ranking per group, and a NULL result when there is no second value.
questions.prompt: For each department that has employees, return department and second_highest_salary: the second-highest distinct salary in that department.

questions.title: Next-month retention by signup cohort
questions.difficultyWhy: Cohort assignment, a relative calendar month, an observation cutoff and decimal ratios.
questions.prompt: Group shoppers into cohorts by signup month. A shopper is retained if they placed a non-cancelled order in the calendar month after their signup month. Return cohort_month, cohort_size, retained and retention_pct.

questions.title: Longest login streak
questions.difficultyWhy: Gaps-and-islands: deduplicate, derive a group key from dates minus row numbers, then aggregate twice.
questions.prompt: For each shopper in app_logins, return shopper_id and longest_streak: the most consecutive calendar days on which they logged in.

questions.title: Salary at the time of each review
questions.difficultyWhy: As-of lookup over half-open, open-ended intervals with overlapping bad data and missing history.
questions.prompt: For every performance review, return review_id, employee_id, review_date and salary_at_review: the salary from salary_history whose period contains the review date.

questions.title: Detect overlapping history periods
questions.difficultyWhy: Interval-overlap logic on a self-join with half-open bounds, open ends and no duplicate pairs.
questions.prompt: Within one employee's salary_history, periods must not overlap. Return employee_id, first_from and second_from for every pair of overlapping periods, where first_from is the earlier valid_from.

questions.title: Management chain for every employee
questions.difficultyWhy: A recursive walk of a hierarchy with several roots, carrying depth and a path string.
questions.prompt: Starting from every employee with no manager, return id, name, level (top = 1) and chain: the names from the top of the hierarchy down to the employee, joined by ' > '.

questions.title: Median order value by region
questions.difficultyWhy: No MEDIAN in SQLite: needs order totals, per-group positions and correct even/odd handling.
questions.prompt: An order's value is the sum of quantity × unit_price over its lines. For non-cancelled orders, return region and median_order_value per shopper region.

questions.title: Build a region history from snapshots
questions.difficultyWhy: Gaps-and-islands with NULL as a real value, non-adjacent repeats, and LEAD for end dates (an SCD Type 2 build).
questions.prompt: shopper_snapshots records each shopper's region at month end. Return shopper_id, region, valid_from and valid_to — one row per unbroken run of the same region.

questions.title: Reconcile orders, payments and refunds
questions.difficultyWhy: Three child tables at different grains, classification rules, and NULL/rounding handling.
questions.prompt: For every non-cancelled order, compute order_total (lines), paid (payments) and refunded (refunds), and classify payment_check: 'unpaid' when nothing was paid, 'underpaid' when paid < order_total, 'overpaid' when paid > order_total, otherwise 'ok'. Return id, order_total, paid, refunded and payment_check for orders that are not 'ok'.

questions.title: Design a purchase lookup index
questions.difficultyWhy: Choose equality-prefix and range-key order, preserve a half-open boundary, and satisfy a catalog plus plan contract.
questions.prompt: Harbor Market needs the purchases for shopper 42 on January 4, 2025. Create a full index with exactly (shopper_id, event_kind, event_at), in that order, then return id, event_at and amount for those purchases. The submitted SELECT must use an indexed search through that index.
questions.setupSql:
WITH RECURSIVE n(x) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT x+1 FROM n WHERE x<12000)
INSERT INTO market_query_log
SELECT x,x%97,CASE WHEN x%3=0 THEN 'purchase' ELSE 'view' END,
       datetime('2025-01-01', '+' || x || ' minutes'),x%500 FROM n;
INSERT INTO market_query_log VALUES
(12001,42,'purchase','2025-01-04 00:00:00',700),
(12002,42,'purchase','2025-01-05 00:00:00',701),
(12003,7,'view','2025-01-04 12:00:00',702),
(12004,5,'purchase','2025-01-04 12:00:00',900),
(12005,5,'purchase','2025-01-04 12:00:00',900);
equivalentSolutions:
CREATE INDEX another_name ON market_query_log(shopper_id,event_kind,event_at);WITH found AS (SELECT id,event_at,amount FROM market_query_log
WHERE shopper_id=42 AND event_kind='purchase'
AND event_at>='2025-01-04 00:00:00' AND event_at<'2025-01-05 00:00:00'
ORDER BY event_at,id) SELECT * FROM found ORDER BY event_at,id

CREATE INDEX purchase_lookup ON market_query_log(shopper_id,event_kind,event_at);SELECT id,event_at,amount FROM market_query_log
WHERE 42=shopper_id AND event_kind='purchase'
AND event_at>='2025-01-04 00:00:00' AND event_at<'2025-01-05 00:00:00'
ORDER BY event_at,id

questions.title: Cover the event export
questions.difficultyWhy: Separate filter keys from payload columns and demonstrate covering access while preserving a time boundary.
questions.prompt: Export event_at and amount for shopper 7 on January 4, 2025. Create a full index with exactly (shopper_id, event_at, amount) and make the final query use a covering indexed search.
questions.setupSql:
WITH RECURSIVE n(x) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT x+1 FROM n WHERE x<12000)
INSERT INTO market_query_log
SELECT x,x%97,CASE WHEN x%3=0 THEN 'purchase' ELSE 'view' END,
       datetime('2025-01-01', '+' || x || ' minutes'),x%500 FROM n;
INSERT INTO market_query_log VALUES
(12001,42,'purchase','2025-01-04 00:00:00',700),
(12002,42,'purchase','2025-01-05 00:00:00',701),
(12003,7,'view','2025-01-04 12:00:00',702),
(12004,5,'purchase','2025-01-04 12:00:00',900),
(12005,5,'purchase','2025-01-04 12:00:00',900);
equivalentSolutions:
CREATE INDEX my_cover ON market_query_log(shopper_id,event_at,amount);SELECT event_at,amount FROM market_query_log WHERE shopper_id IN (7)
AND event_at>='2025-01-04 00:00:00' AND event_at<'2025-01-05 00:00:00' ORDER BY event_at,amount

questions.title: Make the event-day filter SARGable
questions.difficultyWhy: Rewrite a function-wrapped timestamp predicate as a half-open range and verify the resulting access.
questions.prompt: The starting approach is SELECT id,event_at,amount FROM market_query_log WHERE date(event_at)='2025-01-04' ORDER BY event_at,id. Rewrite the filter, create a full index on exactly (event_at), and return the same rows using an indexed search.
questions.setupSql:
WITH RECURSIVE n(x) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT x+1 FROM n WHERE x<12000)
INSERT INTO market_query_log
SELECT x,x%97,CASE WHEN x%3=0 THEN 'purchase' ELSE 'view' END,
       datetime('2025-01-01', '+' || x || ' minutes'),x%500 FROM n;
INSERT INTO market_query_log VALUES
(12001,42,'purchase','2025-01-04 00:00:00',700),
(12002,42,'purchase','2025-01-05 00:00:00',701),
(12003,7,'view','2025-01-04 12:00:00',702),
(12004,5,'purchase','2025-01-04 12:00:00',900),
(12005,5,'purchase','2025-01-04 12:00:00',900);

CREATE INDEX event_time ON market_query_log(event_at);SELECT id,event_at,amount FROM market_query_log
WHERE '2025-01-04 00:00:00'<=event_at AND event_at<'2025-01-05 00:00:00' ORDER BY event_at,id

questions.title: Top events without a temporary sort
questions.difficultyWhy: Align equality filtering, two descending sort keys and a deterministic top-N boundary with index traversal.
questions.prompt: Return the eight highest-amount events for shopper 5, breaking ties by larger id first. Build a full index with exactly (shopper_id, amount, id). Require an indexed search and no temporary sorting B-tree in the final plan.
questions.setupSql:
WITH RECURSIVE n(x) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT x+1 FROM n WHERE x<12000)
INSERT INTO market_query_log
SELECT x,x%97,CASE WHEN x%3=0 THEN 'purchase' ELSE 'view' END,
       datetime('2025-01-01', '+' || x || ' minutes'),x%500 FROM n;
INSERT INTO market_query_log VALUES
(12001,42,'purchase','2025-01-04 00:00:00',700),
(12002,42,'purchase','2025-01-05 00:00:00',701),
(12003,7,'view','2025-01-04 12:00:00',702),
(12004,5,'purchase','2025-01-04 12:00:00',900),
(12005,5,'purchase','2025-01-04 12:00:00',900);
equivalentSolutions: CREATE INDEX reverse_walk ON market_query_log(shopper_id,amount,id);SELECT id,amount FROM market_query_log WHERE 5=shopper_id ORDER BY amount DESC,id DESC LIMIT 8

questions.title: Find a truly ordered cart funnel
questions.difficultyWhy: Reason about a three-step sequence, same-cart identity, retry deduplication and an inclusive time limit.
questions.prompt: Find every shopper/cart pair with a view followed by checkout followed by purchase, all for that cart, where purchase occurs within 30 minutes of the view. Return each qualifying pair once.
equivalentSolutions:
WITH ranked_events AS (
 SELECT *,ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY event_key ORDER BY id) AS retry_rank
 FROM market_web_events
), events AS (SELECT * FROM ranked_events WHERE retry_rank=1)
SELECT v.shopper_id,v.cart_id FROM events v
JOIN events c ON c.shopper_id=v.shopper_id AND c.cart_id=v.cart_id AND c.event_type='checkout' AND (c.occurred_at>v.occurred_at OR (c.occurred_at=v.occurred_at AND c.id>v.id))
JOIN events p ON p.shopper_id=v.shopper_id AND p.cart_id=v.cart_id AND p.event_type='purchase' AND (p.occurred_at>c.occurred_at OR (p.occurred_at=c.occurred_at AND p.id>c.id))
WHERE v.event_type='view' AND unixepoch(p.occurred_at)-unixepoch(v.occurred_at)<=1800
GROUP BY v.shopper_id,v.cart_id ORDER BY v.shopper_id,v.cart_id

questions.title: Identify abandoned checkout attempts
questions.difficultyWhy: Use a same-cart anti-join with a temporal deadline and distinguish attempts from shoppers.
questions.prompt: At the fixed observation cutoff 2025-05-03 00:00:00, list each canonical checkout that had no later purchase of the same cart within 30 minutes. Return checkout_id, shopper_id, cart_id and its deadline.

questions.title: Audit conflicting event retries
questions.difficultyWhy: Select a canonical row while retaining multiplicity and detecting retries with conflicting payload.
questions.prompt: Report only retried event keys. Return event_key, the smallest id as canonical_id, the event_type from that canonical row as canonical_type, and the number of additional ingestion rows as retry_count.

questions.title: Sessionize retries and exact boundaries
questions.difficultyWhy: Deduplicate before LAG, flag strict inactivity boundaries and use a row-based running sum with deterministic ties.
questions.prompt: Assign each canonical website event a session_no for its shopper. Return shopper_id, event_id and session_no, in shopper and event order.

questions.title: Attribute session conversion to first touch
questions.difficultyWhy: Combine sessionization, first-touch attribution and an ordered same-cart funnel without counting event rows as sessions.
questions.prompt: For each first-touch channel, count sessions and converted_sessions, then return conversion_pct rounded to two decimals. A converted session contains an ordered view → checkout → purchase of the same cart within that session.

questions.title: Build a replay-safe ledger load
questions.difficultyWhy: Resolve conflicting source versions, preserve newer target records and prove repeated execution is safe.
questions.prompt: Merge market_load_feed into market_ledger. For each external_id choose the highest source version, breaking ties by greatest feed id. Insert missing keys and replace a target only when the source version is at least its version. Return the entire final ledger.

questions.title: Enforce the reservation boundary
questions.difficultyWhy: Filter invalid references and storage types before deduplicating, then enforce equivalent rules for future writes.
questions.prompt: Create safe_reservations with shopper_id, item_id and quantity. Load the latest valid feed row for each shopper/item pair, then return the loaded rows. Valid input has existing shopper and item keys and an integer-stored quantity from 1 through 5.

questions.title: Recover a failed stock allocation
questions.difficultyWhy: Recover both stock and audit effects of a rejected batch, preserve history and apply a valid batch atomically.
questions.prompt: The rejected batch cannot fit available stock: its item 2 request exceeds availability. Demonstrate recovery from a provisional reservation of 2 units of item 1 and a rejected audit entry, then apply only the accepted batch. Return item_id, available and reserved from the final stock table.

questions.title: Measure co-purchased product pairs
questions.difficultyWhy: Self-join a bridge table while eliminating self-pairs, mirrored pairs and quantity weighting.
questions.prompt: Find unordered pairs of distinct products appearing together in delivered orders. Return the smaller item id as item_a, the larger as item_b, and the number of shared orders.
equivalentSolutions:
SELECT a.item_id AS item_a,b.item_id AS item_b,COUNT(DISTINCT a.order_id) AS shared_orders
FROM order_lines a JOIN order_lines b ON b.order_id=a.order_id AND a.item_id<b.item_id
JOIN sales_orders o ON o.id=a.order_id WHERE o.status='delivered'
GROUP BY a.item_id,b.item_id ORDER BY shared_orders DESC,item_a,item_b

questions.title: Find shoppers in every category
questions.difficultyWhy: Express relational division over a dynamic category universe, respecting delivered-order membership.
questions.prompt: Return shoppers who bought at least one item from every distinct category currently in catalog_items, considering only delivered orders.
questions.setupSql:
INSERT INTO sales_orders VALUES(9101,1,'2025-04-10','delivered','2025-04-12'),(9102,2,'2025-04-10','cancelled',NULL);
INSERT INTO order_lines VALUES(9101,7,1,25),(9102,1,1,39);
equivalentSolutions: SELECT s.id AS shopper_id,s.name FROM shoppers s JOIN sales_orders o ON o.shopper_id=s.id JOIN order_lines l ON l.order_id=o.id JOIN catalog_items c ON c.id=l.item_id WHERE o.status='delivered' GROUP BY s.id,s.name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT c.category)=(SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT category) FROM catalog_items) ORDER BY shopper_id

questions.title: Compare category audience overlap
questions.difficultyWhy: Reduce the bridge to shopper/category membership before computing set intersections and unions.
questions.prompt: For each alphabetically ordered pair of categories sharing at least one delivered-order shopper, return shared_buyers, union_buyers and jaccard = shared / union rounded to three decimals.

questions.title: Parse malformed product codes
questions.difficultyWhy: Validate the entire token before extracting typed fields; CAST alone accepts malformed numeric prefixes.
questions.prompt: Normalize raw_code by trimming ASCII spaces and uppercasing it. Keep only codes of the exact form HM-DDDD-AA, where DDDD is four ASCII digits representing 1–9999 and AA is two ASCII letters. Return import_id, integer item_number and uppercase region.

questions.title: Normalize contact import collisions
questions.difficultyWhy: Apply an explicit normalization and validity contract before grouping, without collapsing meaningful aliases.
questions.prompt: Find duplicate valid emails after lowercasing and trimming outer ASCII spaces, tabs, carriage returns and line feeds. Return normalized_email, source_rows and the smallest source id as first_id.

questions.title: Parse money into exact integer cents
questions.difficultyWhy: Validate sign, decimal grammar and digit limits, then compute cents without permissive casts or floating-point rounding.
questions.prompt: For every import row, parse raw_amount into cents or NULL and label status valid or invalid. Trim outer ASCII spaces. Accept an optional leading + or -, one to six ASCII whole-number digits, and optionally a decimal point followed by one or two ASCII digits.

questions.title: Checkout review 1: establish the baseline
questions.difficultyWhy: Aggregate at session grain, assign cross-midnight sessions to their start day, and distinguish sessions from shoppers.
questions.prompt: Harbor Market is investigating checkout reliability. First build a daily session baseline: session_date, sessions, distinct shoppers and returning_sessions. A returning session is any session numbered greater than 1 for that shopper in this observation dataset.

questions.title: Checkout review 2: locate funnel drop-off
questions.difficultyWhy: Build nested ordered-funnel populations before calculating stage-to-stage losses.
questions.prompt: Continue the checkout review by returning three rows: view, checkout and purchase. Count sessions reaching each ordered stage. Return stage_no (1–3), stage, sessions and dropoff from the preceding stage.

questions.title: Checkout review 3: measure the delay tail
questions.difficultyWhy: Choose a deterministic successful attempt per session and calculate a discrete percentile at the correct grain.
questions.prompt: For each first-touch channel with converted sessions, report converted_sessions, avg_seconds from checkout to purchase rounded to two decimals, and the nearest-rank p90_seconds.

questions.title: Checkout review 4: find later recoveries
questions.difficultyWhy: Link abandoned sessions to a later same-cart purchase within a bounded window without multiplying attempts.
questions.prompt: An abandoned session contains checkout but no full ordered conversion. Find abandoned sessions with a same-cart purchase in a strictly later session within 24 hours of a checkout in the abandoned session. Return shopper_id, abandoned_session, recovery_session and recovery_minutes.

questions.title: Checkout review 5: prioritize channel fixes
questions.difficultyWhy: Reconcile session, abandonment and recovery populations before ranking unresolved losses with shared ranks for ties.
questions.prompt: Prioritize channels by unrecovered abandoned sessions. For each session’s first-touch channel, return sessions, abandoned_sessions, recovered_sessions, unrecovered_sessions and priority_rank.

questions.title: Predict: members with and without bookings
questions.difficultyWhy: Track row membership, NULLs, ties and the explicit ordering in a small fixture.
questions.prompt: Predict every member id and matched fee. Members without bookings must remain in the LEFT JOIN result.

questions.title: Predict: unknown credits in a filter
questions.difficultyWhy: Track row membership, NULLs, ties and the explicit ordering in a small fixture.
questions.prompt: Predict which member ids survive a comparison with 80. Return one numeric id per row.

questions.title: Predict: count rows or known values?
questions.difficultyWhy: Track row membership, NULLs, ties and the explicit ordering in a small fixture.
questions.prompt: Predict one summary per team. Count every member separately from members whose credits are known.

questions.title: Predict: positions and shared ranks
questions.difficultyWhy: Track row membership, NULLs, ties and the explicit ordering in a small fixture.
questions.prompt: Predict row positions, ranks and dense ranks for members with known credits. The position breaks ties by id; the ranks compare credits only.

questions.title: Predict: a frame that includes peers
questions.difficultyWhy: Track row membership, NULLs, ties and the explicit ordering in a small fixture.
questions.prompt: Predict the two running totals. RANGE includes every peer at the current credit value; ROWS walks the deterministic credits,id ordering.

questions.title: Predict: the previous member within a team
questions.difficultyWhy: Track row membership, NULLs, ties and the explicit ordering in a small fixture.
questions.prompt: Predict each member’s previous credits within their team, in id order. A team’s first member has no previous row.

questions.title: Debug: find members with unknown credits
questions.difficultyWhy: Identify the logical mistake and write a correction that also handles unseen edge cases.
questions.prompt: Fix the filter to return ids of members whose credits are unknown, ordered by id.
questions.extraMutation: UPDATE studio_members SET credits=NULL WHERE id=2;
equivalentSolutions: SELECT id FROM studio_members WHERE NOT (credits IS NOT NULL) ORDER BY id

questions.title: Debug: retain members without paid bookings
questions.difficultyWhy: Identify the logical mistake and write a correction that also handles unseen edge cases.
questions.prompt: Return every member and each of their bookings with fee at least 25. Members without a qualifying booking need one NULL fee row. Order by member id then booking id.
equivalentSolutions: SELECT m.id,b.fee FROM studio_members m LEFT JOIN (SELECT * FROM studio_bookings WHERE fee>=25) b ON b.member_id=m.id ORDER BY m.id,b.id

questions.title: Debug: count zero bookings correctly
questions.difficultyWhy: Identify the logical mistake and write a correction that also handles unseen edge cases.
questions.prompt: Return one row per member with the number of matching bookings, including bookings whose fee is NULL. Members without bookings need zero.
equivalentSolutions: SELECT m.id,(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM studio_bookings b WHERE b.member_id=m.id) AS bookings FROM studio_members m ORDER BY m.id

questions.title: Debug: the second distinct credit balance
questions.difficultyWhy: Identify the logical mistake and write a correction that also handles unseen edge cases.
questions.prompt: Return the second-highest distinct known credit balance once. Return no rows if fewer than two distinct known balances exist.
equivalentSolutions: WITH r AS (SELECT credits,DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY credits DESC) AS n FROM studio_members WHERE credits IS NOT NULL) SELECT DISTINCT credits FROM r WHERE n=2 ORDER BY credits DESC

questions.title: Debug: April bookings at the boundary
questions.difficultyWhy: Identify the logical mistake and write a correction that also handles unseen edge cases.
questions.prompt: Return all booking ids in April 2026, ordered by id. Use a half-open month interval so May 1 is excluded.
equivalentSolutions: SELECT id FROM studio_bookings WHERE '2026-04-01' <= booked_at AND NOT (booked_at >= '2026-05-01') ORDER BY id

questions.title: Debug: the last balance in each team
questions.difficultyWhy: Identify the logical mistake and write a correction that also handles unseen edge cases.
questions.prompt: For each member, return the credits of the team’s last member in id order. Keep NULL if that last member has unknown credits. Return rows ordered by id.
equivalentSolutions: SELECT m.id,(SELECT x.credits FROM studio_members x WHERE x.team=m.team ORDER BY x.id DESC LIMIT 1) AS last_credits FROM studio_members m ORDER BY m.id

questions.title: Capacity 1: current regional totals
questions.difficultyWhy: Combine explicit time boundaries with grain-aware aggregation while preserving missing groups.
questions.prompt: Summarize active capacity on the snapshot date for every region, including empty regions as zero. Exclude sites without a mapped region. Order by region id.

questions.title: Capacity 2: retain missing and unmapped sites
questions.difficultyWhy: Combine explicit time boundaries with grain-aware aggregation while preserving missing groups.
questions.prompt: Report every site, its region name (NULL for unmapped sites), and active capacity on the snapshot date. Missing active capacity is zero. Order by site id.

questions.title: Capacity 3: the next delivery date and all ties
questions.difficultyWhy: Combine explicit time boundaries with grain-aware aggregation while preserving missing groups.
questions.prompt: For each site, find the earliest delivery date on or after the snapshot date and sum every delivery tied on that date. Use NULL date and zero units when none exists. Order by site id.

questions.title: Capacity 4: reconcile capacity and incoming supply
questions.difficultyWhy: Combine explicit time boundaries with grain-aware aggregation while preserving missing groups.
questions.prompt: For every site report snapshot capacity and the sum of deliveries from April 1 through April 30 inclusive in separate columns. Avoid multiplying current capacity by the number of deliveries. Order by site id.

questions.title: Capacity 5: project regional capacity at month end
questions.difficultyWhy: Combine explicit time boundaries with grain-aware aggregation while preserving missing groups.
questions.prompt: Project every region’s capacity on April 30, 2026: sum capacity records valid on April 30 plus incremental deliveries arriving April 1 through April 30 inclusive. Exclude unmapped sites and include empty regions as zero. Assume deliveries remain available through the cutoff. Order by region id.
